cases.name: zero-traffic-ratio
cases.prompt:
Our 'error %' stat panel for the canary service shows NaN every night when it gets zero requests:

sum(rate(errors_total{svc="canary"}[5m])) / sum(rate(requests_total{svc="canary"}[5m]))

Give me a version that never yields NaN or +Inf, and say what the panel will show during zero-traffic periods with your version.
cases.trap: Model wraps everything in `or vector(0)` (reporting healthy 0% when nothing is measured) or adds a tiny epsilon to the denominator without explaining the semantics.
expectations: Guards the denominator so zero is excluded, e.g. (sum(rate(requests_total{...}[5m])) > 0) or an equivalent filter.
States that during zero traffic the guarded query returns no data (empty result) rather than a number.
negative_expectations: Does not claim the guarded query returns 0 during zero traffic.
Does not rely solely on `or vector(0)` as the fix.
